column1: # Nordlander & Lind 2017, A&A 607, A75 -- Table A.1 "Line data for spectral lines used in the abundance analyses"
# Transcribed VERBATIM from the PUBLISHED A&A full-text table
#   https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/full_html/2017/11/aa30427-17/T2.html   (retrieved 2026-09-03)
# Cross-checked row-for-row against the arXiv copy arXiv:1708.01949v2 (PDF text layer): IDENTICAL on
# every column of all 55 rows. Two copies of one paper are NOT interchangeable in general (RYA-1110),
# so both were read; here they agree.
# Notes (verbatim): "Only lines used in the spectrum analyses are listed."
#   (a) Uncertainties (90%) to the transition probabilities are taken from Kelleher & Podobedova (2008),
#       when available.
#   (b) Multiplet components with identical wavelength have been merged. We adopt the wavelength measured
#       from the solar spectrum by Brault & Noyes (1983), and the oscillator strength has been adjusted
#       accordingly.
# gf references (verbatim): (1) Wiese et al. (1969); (2) TOPbase: Mendoza et al. (1995) and C. Mendoza,
#   W. Eissner, M. Le Dourneuf, & C. J. Zeippen (unpublished); (3) Davidson et al. (1990);
#   (4) Vujnovic et al. (2002); (5) Tachiev & Froese Fischer (2002); (6) Kurucz (2012, online data;
#   http://kurucz.harvard.edu/atoms/1300/).
# Wavelengths are AIR -- INCLUDING the 2103-2660 A ultraviolet rows. The paper never states its
# medium, so this is MEASURED, not assumed from convention: the Ritz identity E_up = E_low + hc/lambda
# is single-valued per upper level to 0.00037 eV when the column is read as air and only 0.00167 eV
# when read as vacuum (control C4 in scripts/rya1173_build_asplund_al_lineset.py). 123349.6 A carries
# footnote b.
